experiment_description: Central concept tested: a superconducting quantum annealing processor is operated as an analog-digital quantum computer by using independent “multicolor” annealing lines so that auxiliary source qubits implement programmable single-qubit state preparation, target qubits evolve under a time-independent analog Hamiltonian, and auxiliary detector qubits implement programmable-basis readout. The single-qubit characterization uses independent three-qubit source-target-detector systems on a 1178-qubit D-Wave Advantage2-type quantum annealing processor with six low-frequency annealing lines, each line controlling an anneal parameter s. For each source-target-detector triplet, all qubits start at s=0; the source qubit is forward-annealed to s=1 in a polarizing flux bias and the bias is then removed; the target qubit is brought to a fixed operating point with transverse splitting Delta/h=1.0 GHz and no programmed longitudinal field; the source is rapidly quenched back to s=0 to define the target initial state; after a variable free-evolution time t under H0=-(Delta/2) sigma_z, the detector qubit is rapidly annealed to s=1 and its flux state is measured. Source and detector static flux biases are independently swept from -200 microPhi0 to +200 microPhi0 to map the prepared Bloch vector n_s=(sin(theta_s)cos(phi_s), sin(theta_s)sin(phi_s), cos(theta_s)) and the detector measurement vector n_d=(sin(theta_d)cos(phi_d), sin(theta_d)sin(phi_d), cos(theta_d)). Magnetization data are taken as 1000-shot QPU calls for each t; short-time overlap between initialization and detection is excluded, and fits use the Larmor-precession/decoherence model over the stated fitting window. The fitted observable is <sigma_{n_d}>, where sigma_{n_d}=R_{theta_d,phi_d} sigma_z R^{-1}_{theta_d,phi_d}. The model used for extraction is <sigma_{n_d}>=cos(theta_d)[1-exp(-(t-t0)/T1)(1-cos(theta_s))]+sin(theta_d)sin(theta_s)cos[Delta(t-t0)/hbar+phi_s-phi_d]exp(-(t-t0)/T2), with T2=(1/(2T1)+1/T_phi)^(-1); t0 is the initialization time, T1 is the relaxation time, T_phi is the pure dephasing time, and hbar is the reduced Planck constant. The spatial/statistical scope is the median over 124 independent source-target-detector triplets distributed on the processor, after calibration of per-line delays, per-qubit anneal offsets, and per-qubit flux biases to align the degeneracy point and Larmor phase.

single_qubit_relaxation_time_T1_ns.description: Median relaxation time extracted from the single-target-qubit arbitrary-basis Larmor-precession fits across the calibrated source-target-detector triplets.

single_qubit_pure_dephasing_time_Tphi_ns.description: Median pure dephasing time extracted from the single-target-qubit arbitrary-basis Larmor-precession fits across the calibrated source-target-detector triplets.

source_and_detector_polar_angle_tuning.description: Whether the source and detector flux-bias controls allowed independent continuous tuning of the target preparation and readout polar angles over the Bloch sphere polar interval.

experiment_description: Central concept tested: the same multicolor analog-digital annealing protocol should remain usable when target-target couplings are left on during initialization and readout, so that two-qubit analog evolution can be measured in more than one basis. The experiment uses pairs of target qubits q1 and q2 on the 1178-qubit superconducting annealing processor, each target having a distinct source qubit and a distinct detector qubit controlled by separate annealing-line classes. All target qubits are operated at Delta/h=1.0 GHz with site detunings deltaDelta_i=0 and no programmed longitudinal fields. The two-target effective Hamiltonian in the weak-coupling rotating-wave regime is H_2Q=(J/4)(sigma_x1 sigma_x2+sigma_y1 sigma_y2), where J is the programmed exchange coupling energy. The protocol prepares product states using source-qubit pi/2 or pi pulses, evolves for variable time t over the plotted 0-30 ns window, and reads either sigma_x-basis or sigma_z-basis magnetizations using detector-qubit bias settings. Measurements include configurations with J/h=0, J/h=0.30 GHz, and J/h=0.15 GHz in the main characterization, with supplementary sigma_z-basis fits also varying J/h over 0.09, 0.15, 0.30, and 0.60 GHz. Magnetizations and the correlator <sigma_z1 sigma_z2> are averaged over 2000 shots for each time point in the main figure; for the fitted sigma_z exchange data, two 1000-shot calls with opposite source polarizing biases are combined to suppress state-preparation and measurement bias. The relaxation of <sigma_z1 sigma_z2> and the dephasing of the oscillatory difference <sigma_z1>-<sigma_z2> are fit to an independent-noise two-qubit Lindblad model with identical per-qubit T1 and T_phi, using expressions such as <sigma_z1>=1-exp(-t/T1)[1+exp(-t/T_phi)cos(Jt/hbar)], <sigma_z2>=1-exp(-t/T1)[1-exp(-t/T_phi)cos(Jt/hbar)], and <sigma_z1 sigma_z2>=1-2exp(-t/T1). The quoted fitted medians are obtained from 62 different target-qubit pairs for the sigma_z-basis exchange condition with J/h=0.30 GHz.

two_qubit_relaxation_time_T1_ns.description: Median per-qubit relaxation time extracted from two-target-qubit spin-exchange data using the open-system model.

two_qubit_pure_dephasing_time_Tphi_ns.description: Median pure dephasing time extracted from the two-target-qubit spin-exchange oscillations using the open-system model.

two_qubit_total_dephasing_time_T2_ns.description: Total single-qubit coherence time derived from the fitted two-target-qubit relaxation and pure-dephasing parameters using T2=(1/(2T1)+1/T_phi)^(-1).

experiment_description: Central concept tested: after source-qubit preparation and detector-qubit readout, a large chain of target qubits in a quantum annealer can be used as an analog simulator of coherent many-body dynamics; in the weak-coupling regime the target Hamiltonian is described by an effective XY model or, equivalently for the clean periodic chain, by a transverse-field Ising model whose single-excitation dispersion can be extracted from space-time-resolved magnetization. The experiment embeds a periodic one-dimensional chain of L=56 target qubits on the 1178-qubit processor, with each target coupled to a distinct source and detector qubit; four annealing-line color classes are assigned to target qubits and the remaining two to source and detector qubits. The target chain is programmed with uniform transverse splitting Delta/h=2.0 GHz, zero site detuning deltaDelta_i=0, nearest-neighbor periodic exchange coupling J/h=-0.60 GHz, and no longitudinal fields. A single target site is prepared in |+> by a source-qubit pi/2 operation while the rest of the chain is left in the target ground-state basis, the chain evolves for variable detector delay corresponding to normalized time |J|t/hbar spanning the plotted range, and all targets are read out in the sigma_x basis by detector qubits. The spatial scope is the full 56-site periodic ring; magnetization maps are averaged over all possible locations of the initially excited qubit and over the chain’s site-order-reversal symmetry, with each time/location measurement obtained from QPU shot averages. A two-dimensional Fourier transform over target-site index and evolution time is used to extract the magnetization spectral ridge. In the formula result, k is the quasimomentum in the first Brillouin zone [-pi,pi], Delta is the target transverse energy splitting, J is the nearest-neighbor exchange energy, E(k) is the positive or negative single-particle excitation energy, h is Planck’s constant, and hbar=h/(2pi).

sigma_x_chain_dispersion_relation_energy.description: Empirical single-paramagnon dispersion relation extracted from the space-time Fourier transform of the sigma_x magnetization in the clean periodic chain.

coherent_propagation_normalized_time_low.description: Lower-bound normalized evolution time over which coherent chain propagation is inferred under the clean-chain analog-digital protocol.

experiment_description: Central concept tested: the multicolor analog-digital protocol on a quantum annealer should measure a different dynamical correlator when the same clean target-chain analog evolution is initialized and read out in the energy basis rather than the transverse basis, allowing extraction of the energy-difference spectral structure of a periodic spin chain. The experiment embeds a periodic one-dimensional chain of L=124 target qubits on the 1178-qubit processor, with each target having a distinct source and detector qubit. Four annealing-line color classes control the target chain and two separate line classes control source and detector qubits. The uniform target parameters are Delta/h=2.0 GHz, nearest-neighbor periodic exchange coupling J/h=-0.60 GHz, zero site detuning deltaDelta_i=0, and no programmed longitudinal fields. A single target site is prepared in |1> by a source-qubit pi pulse, the target chain evolves under the fixed clean-chain Hamiltonian for detector delays spanning the plotted normalized-time range |J|t/hbar, and all targets are measured in the sigma_z basis using detector-qubit readout. The spatial scope is the complete 124-site periodic ring; magnetization-derived excitation probabilities are averaged over all initially excited locations and over the chain’s bracelet symmetry, with QPU shot averaging for each time point. The measured field analyzed is the excitation probability rho(n,t)=(1-<sigma_z(n,t)>)/2, and a two-dimensional Fourier transform over site n and time t is used to locate the intensity ridge. In the formula result, k is quasimomentum in [-pi,pi], J is the nearest-neighbor exchange energy, h is Planck’s constant, and f(k) is the frequency of the Fourier-transform intensity peak.

sigma_z_chain_fourier_peak_frequency_Hz.description: Empirical Fourier-transform peak frequency of the excitation-probability dynamics for the clean periodic chain measured in the sigma_z basis.

coherent_propagation_distance_qubits_low.description: Lower-bound propagation distance in lattice sites inferred for the clean-chain sigma_z excitation dynamics before loss of coherent propagation.

experiment_description: Central concept tested: the analog-digital quantum annealing protocol can intentionally program site-dependent target-qubit detunings in an effective XY chain and use arbitrary-basis initialization/readout to probe disorder-induced Anderson localization through the persistence of a spin-density-wave imbalance. The experiment uses a periodic one-dimensional chain of L=124 target qubits on the 1178-qubit processor, with each target assigned a distinct source and detector qubit. The clean target parameters are transverse splitting Delta/h=2.0 GHz, nearest-neighbor exchange coupling J/h=0.20 GHz, and no programmed longitudinal field. Odd-indexed target qubits are prepared in |1> by source-qubit pi pulses to create the staggered initial configuration |1010...>, while even-indexed target qubits are left unexcited; all targets are then evolved under a fixed disordered chain Hamiltonian and measured in the sigma_z basis. Disorder is applied by programming per-qubit anneal offsets that implement detunings deltaDelta_i drawn uniformly from [-J W/2, J W/2], where W is the dimensionless disorder strength; unwanted coupling changes due to the same anneal offsets are compensated by reprogramming Jij values. The measured disorder strengths include W=0, 2, 4, and 8 for time traces over normalized time Jt/hbar spanning the plotted window, with QPU data averaged over 20 independent disorder realizations. The imbalance is computed from excitation probabilities as I(t)=[p_odd(t)-p_even(t)]/[p_odd(t)+p_even(t)], where p_odd=(1/L) sum_{i=1}^{L/2}[1-<sigma_z_{2i-1}>] and p_even=(1/L) sum_{i=1}^{L/2}[1-<sigma_z_{2i}>]. The long-time summary quantity I_tilde is the QPU imbalance averaged over normalized times Jt/hbar from 6*pi to 8*pi, and its small-W dependence is fit to a quadratic scaling form.

small_disorder_average_imbalance_scaling.description: Empirical small-disorder scaling of the time-averaged spin-density-wave imbalance in the disordered periodic chain.
